title: Fair prices or market prices?
hook: Charge each buyer the harm it does to others. Is that what a market would charge?

knows: raising prices on over-demanded items until each buyer gets a preferred item clears a matching market (prices-sort-the-buyers)
the VCG rule: pay the harm you cause others (pay-for-the-harm-you-do)
doesNotKnow: that charging each buyer the harm they cause gives exactly the market-clearing prices found by raising prices

misconception: Prices from a fairness rule (pay the harm) and prices from supply and demand are unrelated.
objective: The learner can compute each buyer's harm (the others' best total without it minus what they get with it) in a 3 × 3 matching market and see that the harms equal the market-clearing prices of the items those buyers get.

Harms: x (gets a) 3, z (gets b) 1, y (gets c) 0. | FC pass 23 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own copy of clearingPrices(), with both the smallest and the largest constricted set raised first: it ends at a 3, b 1, c 0, total 4. Own brute force over integer prices 0-12 finds the unique smallest-total clearing vector, [3,1,0]. Harm on each buyer's own item: x/a 3, z/b 1, y/c 0, which equals the column prices. The difference does not touch the claim; the builder should recount or drop the figure.

claims.text: In matching markets like this, harm (VCG) prices always clear the market, and are the lowest prices that do.
claims.source: Theorem: Leonard (1983), 'Elicitation of honest preferences for the assignment of individuals to positions', Journal of Political Economy 91(3); Easley and Kleinberg (2010) ch. 15 (advanced section); Kern, Manthey and Uetz, arXiv 1604.04157. Fact-checker confirms the exact statement. | FC pass 23 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Leonard (1983) and E&K ch. 15 were NOT opened (every scholarly host was unreachable through the proxy); the theorem (VCG prices = the minimum Walrasian prices in assignment markets; also Demange-Gale-Sotomayor 1986) is from my own knowledge, confident. It does not rest on that alone. In my own randomized test (fc23/vcg.mjs, vcg4.mjs), across 3,000 random 3x3 markets (values 0-8) and 150 random 4x4 markets (values 0-6), VCG prices always cleared, and no integer clearing vector had any price below VCG. That is 0 counterexamples, so VCG was the componentwise minimum every time. Reveal footnote (line 130) matches.

Reveal footnote; Demo.tsx V. | FC pass 23 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Reveal footnote reads 'Invented values.' Demo.tsx V is a hard-coded table taken from the brief, with no real-world referent claimed.

recall.question: In a matching market, removing buyer Q would let the others gain $5 in total. Q gets item k in the best assignment. What is k's lowest market-clearing price?
options: It cannot be told without the full supply and demand
recall.why: Q's harm to the others is $5, and in such markets the harm a buyer causes is the lowest clearing price of the item it gets.
